question: When two anonymous observations preserve the same frozen sibling role, which local critical-center correspondences and edit motifs remain invariant compared with matched role-broken controls?

alignment.coordinateNormalization: observation-region normalized, then centroid centered and isotropically RMS scaled
alignment.transformSelection: label-blind; maximize mutual matched fraction, then minimize median spatial displacement, then mean signature edit, then fixed transform order

editAtoms.label: median displacement of matched critical centers
fraction of matched centers switching endpoint/junction kind
fraction of matched centers changing arm degree
mean absolute change in endpoint-target arm count
mean absolute change in junction-target arm count
mean absolute change in unresolved arm count
fraction of matched centers changing full local arm signature
whether best label-blind center-cloud alignment requires a non-identity transform
whether best alignment requires a 90/270-degree quarter turn

motifDiscovery.pairRate: matched centers with motif divided by all matched centers in that pair

trainDiscovery.familyPairBalancedEffect: mean rank-biserial effect across frozen physical-family pairs
trainDiscovery.continuousEffect: positive means edit magnitude is smaller in role-preserving pairs
trainDiscovery.motifEffect: positive means motif rate is higher in role-preserving pairs
trainDiscovery.null: shuffle preserved/broken labels within each physical-family pair while preserving positive count

transfer.strongTransferGate: same effect sign in holdout and control and each absolute transfer effect at least 25% of train

interpretationLimits.meaning: V4 aligns actual critical-center coordinates and local arm signatures. It can test endpoint/junction insertion, deletion, movement, kind/degree/signature changes and orientation/reflection invariance, but cannot identify a specific center-to-center branch edge because the parent ledger stores arm destination classes rather than target center IDs.
